name: New Democracy
summary: New Democracy is Mao Zedong's theory that the revolution in a colonial, semi-colonial and semi-feudal country must pass through a democratic stage before socialism. The stage is a joint dictatorship of the revolutionary classes (workers, peasants, petty and national bourgeoisie) led by the working class, with land to the tiller, state ownership of big banks and monopolistic enterprises, protection of non-monopoly private capital, and a national, scientific and mass culture.
scope: Mao Zedong's theory as set out in On New Democracy (1940) and On Coalition Government (1945), as the programme of the Chinese Communist Party for the democratic stage of the revolution. It does not cover later Maoist doctrine (continuing revolution, the Cultural Revolution), the socialist stage, or other parties named New Democracy.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: The programme makes land the private property of peasants and allows a rich peasant economy.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The programme guarantees freedom of political conviction and religious belief and demands revocation of laws that suppress them.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: The programme calls for organising underground armed forces for uprisings in Japanese-occupied areas and for a people's war.

bound-labor.rationale: The essay commits the new-democratic republic to abolishing feudal relations in the rural areas.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The essay holds that capitalism is dying, 'like the sun setting beyond the western hills', and will soon be relegated to the museum.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The essay describes imperialism as moribund capitalism that must seize colonies and drags the world into a second imperialist war, citing Lenin's analysis.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The essay treats imperialist rule of a colony as the enemy of independence and development.

class-collaboration.rationale: The 1945 programme has labour and capital work together in the new-democratic stage while stating that their contradiction remains and has only to be adjusted.

collective-farming.rationale: The text says socialist agriculture will not be established at this stage and land goes into peasants' private ownership, though cooperatives with socialist elements may grow from it.

colonial-socialism-democratic-stage.rationale: The essay says the revolution in a colonial, semi-colonial and semi-feudal country must run in two stages, democracy first and then socialism.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The essay is an argument for ending colonial and semi-colonial status and imperialist exploitation.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: New-democratic culture is scientific, stands for objective truth and opposes superstitious ideas.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The programme promises unemployment relief and social insurance for workers.

defeat-communism.rationale: The essay attacks the campaigns to 'restrict', 'corrode' and 'combat' communism as mistakes that will destroy their authors.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The essay calls the Soviet-type republic under the dictatorship of the proletariat the coming dominant form for industrial countries, but New Democracy itself is a joint dictatorship of several classes.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The programme has women participate on an equal footing in all useful work and secures equality of men and women.

dominated-front.rationale: Revolutions in colonies and semi-colonies are said to be allies of the socialist world front against imperialism.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The programme calls for a consolidated progressive tax.

gradual-change.rationale: The essay says there is no construction without destruction and that reactionary culture and feudal forces must be swept away.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Mao says the republic must be new-democratic not only in politics but also in its economy, with state enterprises and land reform.

land-redistribution.rationale: Mao's programme confiscates landlord land and distributes it to peasants with little or no land under 'land to the tiller'.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The programme turns land over to the private ownership of peasants, not to the community or nation.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Mao cites Marx that social being determines consciousness and treats culture as a reflection of politics and economics.

minority-language-support.rationale: Minorities' spoken and written languages, customs and religious beliefs must be respected.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The programme says minority nationalities should be granted autonomous rights and may form their own armies for their emancipation.

national-self-determination.rationale: The essay makes an independent society of China the aim of the first stage, and the 1945 report endorses the right to self-determination of all nationalities in China.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state owns key enterprises, confiscates landlord land and regulates capital, far beyond defence and justice.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The programme calls for outlawing bureaucrat-capital, the privileged capital of landlords, bankers and compradors.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Communist Party leads through the working class, yet the 1945 report says one-party government must not be attempted in the New Democracy stage, so the record runs both ways.

party-controls-media.rationale: The 1945 programme calls freedom of speech and press among the people's most important freedoms and demands the abolition of the secret service and repressive laws.

party-own-road.rationale: Marxism's universal truth must take a definite national form and not be applied as a mere formula.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The essay identifies the feudal forces as a main enemy to be overthrown and feudal relations as something to abolish.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The essay says to respect China's history and keep its democratic essence while rejecting its feudal dross.

property-franchise.rationale: Suffrage is to be universal and equal irrespective of property or education.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private capital is protected where it does not dominate the people's livelihood, but landlord land and bureaucrat-capital are confiscated or outlawed, so property is not treated as very hard to override.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Private property is protected where it benefits the people and does not dominate their livelihood.

public-ownership.rationale: On New Democracy has the state own the big banks and the monopolistic or very large enterprises, such as railways and airlines, whether Chinese- or foreign-owned.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The programme demands freedom of religious belief and repeal of laws suppressing it.

racial-franchise.rationale: Universal equal suffrage irrespective of creed and the equality of all nationalities in China rule out limiting the vote to one ethnic group.

reason-over-faith.rationale: New-democratic culture is scientific and opposed to superstition, though Communists may ally with religious people in politics.

regulate-corporations.rationale: 'Regulation of capital' is named as the main principle of the economy, so that private capital cannot dominate the people's livelihood.

restore-past-order.rationale: The essay says youth should be guided to look forward not backward and warns against eulogizing the past at the expense of the present.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The programme guarantees freedom of religious belief and says minorities' religious beliefs must be respected.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The 1945 programme demands recovery of all lost territory, and Mao's notes cite the Cairo Declaration on returning Taiwan.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Mao says the old culture must not be lopped off and its democratic essence must be assimilated.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The programme ensures freedom of marriage and equality between men and women.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The essay calls the Soviet Union a flourishing socialist state in transition from socialism to communism.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Mao says the question of the state is simply the status of the social classes within it, and that every state has an apparatus of power representing one class or another.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State enterprises of a socialist character are to be the leading force of the whole national economy, though private capital outside the people's livelihood is allowed.

state-harmful.rationale: The essay builds a new state and treats every state as an apparatus of one class or alliance of classes, not as unnecessary.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The essay says colonial countries must line up with imperialism or against it and that Soviet assistance is indispensable.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The state is a dictatorship over counter-revolutionaries and traitors, yet the programme demands legal status for all democratic parties and release of political prisoners.

taxation-theft.rationale: The programme replaces exorbitant taxes with a consolidated progressive tax, accepting taxation in principle.

total-state.rationale: The programme leaves room for private and cooperative sectors and guarantees academic freedom and civil liberties.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The texts condemn fascism and praise the Soviet Union as socialist, so they do not equate the two.

unions-good.rationale: The programme guarantees trade union rights and helps workers to organise in order to expand production.

vanguard-party.rationale: The working class became an awakened political force through the influence of the Russian Revolution and under the leadership of the Chinese Communist Party, which alone carried out the agrarian revolution.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The essay says the economy must never be 'privately owned by the few' and that a few capitalists must not dominate the people's livelihood.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Land goes to small peasant owners and ownership by 'the few' is rejected, but the state also holds the large enterprises, so the doctrine points both ways on this statement.

women-suffrage.rationale: The essay calls for really universal and equal suffrage irrespective of sex, creed, property or education.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: Workers and peasants are the basic forces of the revolution and the Communist Party won the peasants as its great ally.

workers-anti-imperialist-capitalist-alli.rationale: The essay says the proletariat's task is a united front with the national bourgeoisie against imperialism.

workers-own-party.rationale: The proletariat became an independent political force under its own party, the Chinese Communist Party.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The essay says imperialism opposes China's development and that capitalist powers depend on colonies and semi-colonies to survive.

missingStatements.text: Private capitalist businesses should be protected during a transitional democratic stage.
missingStatements.rationale: New Democracy protects private capitalist production outside monopolistic sectors during the democratic stage, with socialism left to a later stage.

quotes.text: the republic will neither confiscate capitalist private property in general nor forbid the development of such capitalist production as does not "dominate the livelihood of the people"
freely develop such private capitalist economy as will benefit and not "dominate the livelihood of the people", and to protect all appropriate forms of private property
quotes.where: On Coalition Government, section on the general programme

missingStatements.declined: Theory wording about a revolutionary stage.

notes: Answers rest on Mao's 1940 essay and 1945 report; the later record of the People's Republic is not used. Themes searched in the two texts: economy (ownership, land, tax, labour), government (suffrage, parties, assembly, army), liberty (speech, religion), society (women, minorities, culture), world (imperialism, Soviet Union, UN) and means (revolution, armed struggle, alliances). Ecology, technology and most culture-war and moral statements are not addressed and stay null.
